title: Console: Request Storage Safeguards & PII Redaction Demo — BlueForge Systems
summary: Demo focused on Redwood Console controls for request storage toggles, automatic PII redaction, and audit-friendly logging. Customer wants clear options for ephemeral vs stored requests, KMS integration, and a path for a 30-day pilot with performance guardrails.
next_steps: Maya: share SOC2 + encryption whitepaper and short architecture note (by 2026-07-02)
Connor: provision pilot environment and sample config for ephemeral mode (by 2026-07-07)
BlueForge: provide sample prompt set and expected SLOs for latency/cost (by 2026-07-06)
Schedule follow-up benchmark session with infra team (target week of 2026-07-13)
action_items: Maya Patel: send SOC2 and security pack link by 2026-07-02
Connor Liu: create pilot config (ephemeral + redaction rules), demo scripts, and invite BlueForge to pilot workspace by 2026-07-07
Laura Chen: email sample PII-heavy prompt sets and success criteria by 2026-07-06
transcript: [00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone — thanks for making time, I'll kick us off. we have Connor and Asha from product with me. how's the signal on audio?
[00:10] Marcus Vega: Good here, a little background noise but okay. thanks for doing this.
[00:15] Laura Chen: hey all, excited. we wanted to see how request storage toggles would look, specifically want ephemeral mode and controlled retention for only flagged requests.

[00:30] Connor Liu: great — today we'll walk the Console and then run a quick API demo to show redaction in flight. apologies if some names sound weird, auto transcript sometimes munges K M S into K M S and stuff.
[00:45] Asha Rivera: quick agenda: 1) quick security overview 2) console walkthrough of request storage toggles 3) live example of PII redaction 4) pilot next steps and Q&A.
[01:05] Ibrahim Khan: quick ask — we run in Azure, need to validate our KMS and key rotation, also data residency for EU data. can you confirm?
[01:20] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support customer-managed keys and KMS integrations, plus regional routing. we'll show the KMS UI and the audit logs after the demo.
[01:35] Marcus Vega: okay, and for compliance — SOC 2 + ISO? we need to present to compliance team next week.
[01:45] Maya Patel: we have SOC 2 Type II, yes — i'll share the pack after the call. I'll also include the whitepaper on encryption at rest and in transit.
[02:05] Connor Liu: jumping into the Console — screen share — okay can everyone see the Console? (pause) cool. top-right is the request-storage section under governance.

[02:25] Connor Liu: here we have three modes: store-all, ephemeral, and selective-store. selective-store ties to a policy engine and can be configured with regex and PII detectors. note: the labeling here is a bit different from older docs — sorry if the transcript calls it selective-storey.
[02:50] Laura Chen: does selective-store allow TTL per-request or per-tag?
[02:55] Connor Liu: yes, both. you can set a retention TTL on tags and on the policy itself; the Console exposes per-route overrides too.
[03:10] Samir Patel: and where do the logs go — our security team needs to ingest them into Splunk or our SIEM, not keep them in a public bucket.

[03:20] Asha Rivera: integrations exist for Splunk/Datadog and you can route audit-only logs via our VPC flow to a customer-managed bucket or forwarder. the request-storage is separate from audit logs — audit logs always kept (configurable retention), request payloads follow the storage toggles.
[03:45] Ibrahim Khan: what about PII redaction — is that pre-storage or on read?

[03:50] Connor Liu: we do redaction pre-storage when enabled — it runs a PII classifier + redaction pipeline. you can configure levels, from token masking to full removal. example: credit card numbers → masked, SSNs → removed, names → pseudonymized.
[04:10] Laura Chen: is the PII detector model open to tuning? we have domain-specific identifiers that our detector should catch.
[04:20] Connor Liu: yes, we support custom rules + uploadable regex list and a fine-tuning hook for the PII model. we'll include a sample plugin in the pilot workspace.
[04:35] Marcus Vega: latency impact? redaction sounds costly on token path.

[04:40] Connor Liu: good question — in our benchmarks redaction adds ~5-15ms on avg per request if run inline, we also have async post-process for non-blocking retention where the request is served immediately and payload processed for storage-only purposes. we can show both patterns in pilot.
[05:05] Maya Patel: i'll note that as a tradeoff — inline redaction for strict compliance, async pipeline for lower p99 impact.
[05:20] [05:20] Conversation: (laughter) — somebody says it's like choosing between speed and doing the right thing — classic.
[05:35] Connor Liu: moving to the API demo — i'll run a sample curl with ephemeral mode header X-Redwood-Request-Store: ephemeral and show the logs. run now...
[05:50] Connor Liu: (typing) — okay request sent. transcript shows the original text but the console shows 'ephemeral-true' and no stored payload in the request store grid.
[06:10] Laura Chen: i see the console showing request-id but the payload column is empty — is that expected?
[06:15] Connor Liu: yes that's ephemeral. you can still see metadata (routing, model, latency) but not the prompt/response text when ephemeral mode is on.
[06:30] Marcus Vega: fine — what about selective-store with hold-for-review rule?

[06:35] Connor Liu: we have a policy engine rule set: if PII-confidence > 0.8 OR contains token 'billing' then store to quarantine bucket with TTL 30 days. you can set manual review workflows to release or purge.
[06:55] Ibrahim Khan: can quarantine be in our VPC only? we can't have cross-tenant shared buckets.
[07:00] Asha Rivera: yes — quarantine can be routed to customer-managed storage inside your VPC or to a Private deployment's internal store for air-gapped scenarios.
[07:20] Samir Patel: key rotation and KMS — how are keys used for stored payloads vs audit logs?

[07:25] Connor Liu: stored payloads use envelope encryption with customer-managed keys; audit logs can be optionally encrypted with a different key. key rotation is supported with rewrap operations; we document rotation playbook in the whitepaper.
[07:45] Laura Chen: is there proof of deletion or tamper-evidence for compliance?

[07:50] Maya Patel: yes—we provide deletion records in the audit log with hash confirmation; for Dedicated/Private deployments you can enable WORM on the bucket and we produce tamper evidence entries.
[08:10] Marcus Vega: about exports — our legal team wants an exportable report of redaction rules and actions over time for audits.
[08:20] Connor Liu: Console -> Governance -> Reports -> Retention Actions has an export CSV plus policy snapshots; we'll add BlueForge to a demo report so you can see the format.
[08:40] Laura Chen: can we test false positives/false negatives? we need metrics for redaction accuracy on our domain.
[08:45] Connor Liu: absolutely — pilot includes a validation harness and you can provide labeled examples. we run the eval and produce precision/recall numbers per rule.
[09:05] [09:05] Interruption: an incoming chat — 'Maya: I'll paste the SOC2 link in chat'
[09:20] Maya Patel: sharing: https://redwood.app/security/blueforge-soc2-pack.pdf — folks should have access, i'll follow up with full pack.
[09:35] Ibrahim Khan: nice. can we also restrict Console access by route and scope — RBAC?
[09:40] Asha Rivera: RBAC is role-based with route-level scopes; you can tie to your SSO (SAML/Okta). session MFA can be enforced per role.
[09:55] Marcus Vega: fine — what are limits for the pilot in terms of qps and model selection?

[10:00] Connor Liu: for pilot we can reserve a small Dedicated pool or run in Hosted with burst capacity. we'll size based on your sample traffic; typically pilots aim for 50-200 rps test, we can tune batching and caching.
[10:20] Marcus Vega: and cost implications of selective-store vs ephemeral?

[10:25] Maya Patel: storing requests increases unit cost (storage + retrieval + egress if exported). selective-store reduces taggable volume — Redwood Optimize has suggestions to tune batch sizes and cache to offset cost.
[10:45] Laura Chen: ok, can you walk through an example redaction rule? maybe show the regex editor and a custom classifier hook.

[10:50] Connor Liu: sure — show editor — here's a sample rule: detect domain-specific SKU pattern 'BF-[0-9]{6}' and mask with BF-XXXXXX. we also have a 'custom model endpoint' option where you can send candidate text for a micro-model and get tags back.
[11:15] Samir Patel: that makes sense. can the micro-model run behind our VPC?
[11:20] Connor Liu: yes — for Private deployments you can run the micro-model in your environment and return tags. our webhook supports mTLS.
[11:40] Laura Chen: what happens on restore — if we purge then later need to restore for legal hold?
[11:45] Asha Rivera: we support legal hold policies — items under legal hold are moved and exempted from TTL purge; restore is an admin workflow with audit entries.
[12:05] Ibrahim Khan: small nit — the console UI earlier showed 'policy engine v2' — is that GA?
[12:10] Connor Liu: policy engine v2 is GA for Hosted and Dedicated, Private will get it in the upcoming patch; we'll confirm the timeline in the follow-up notes, might be next month.
[12:30] Marcus Vega: can you also show an example where redaction fails and manual review flow?

[12:35] Connor Liu: yes — simulation: i'll send a prompt with an obfuscated SSN — the detector flags low confidence, it goes to quarantine and creates a review ticket inside the Console. (types) okay ticket created, reviewer can accept or request deletion.
[12:55] Laura Chen: will reviewers see the original text or a redacted preview?
[13:00] Connor Liu: by default reviewer sees a redacted preview with a link that requires additional privileges to unmask — we log unmask events in audit.
[13:15] Maya Patel: big picture — we want to make sure audits are clean for your compliance team and you have guardrails to avoid accidental data retention.
[13:30] Marcus Vega: sounds good. a few logistical Qs — timeline for pilot, SLA, and cost estimate?
[13:35] Maya Patel: quick answer: pilot 4 weeks, we offer limited SLA for pilot; post-pilot pricing for Dedicated/Private depends on capacity. i'll send a ballpark pricing spreadsheet with options.
[13:55] Laura Chen: one more — do you have references for banks/healthcare using these redaction features?
[14:00] Maya Patel: yes — i'll include two references: a mid-size payer and a retail bank (contacts included in the pack), and a case study link in the follow-up email.
[14:15] [14:15] -- 40 minutes of deeper Q&A and console clicks omitted here for brevity, full transcript includes more examples --

[42:20] Connor Liu: returning to recap — we set up pilot with ephemeral mode default, a selective-store policy for billing/PII, KMS integration to your Azure Key Vault, and a weekly benchmark suite to measure redaction latency/accuracy.
[42:40] Laura Chen: that aligns with our needs. please include the evaluation harness and export template so our compliance folks can run through it.
[42:55] Maya Patel: noted — action items captured. i'll follow up with SOC2 + whitepaper, Connor will provision pilot workspace and sample config, Laura will send prompt set.
[43:10] Marcus Vega: schedule the benchmark session — invite my infra lead and security architect. prefer week of July 13.
[43:25] Maya Patel: will do. any final questions?
[43:30] Ibrahim Khan: one last — what's the rollback if redaction rules accidentally delete necessary data?

[43:35] Connor Liu: we keep a hashed audit trail; for Dedicated/Private you can configure soft-delete first and require manual purge. we'll default pilots to soft-delete to avoid accidental permanent removal.
[43:55] Laura Chen: perfect — thanks everyone, helpful session.
[44:05] Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll send materials and schedule the follow-up. bye.
[44:10] Meeting ended
